items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: And then formed a little group of my own. With Barney B. Godd on tenor we were learning in Saxton. And Louie Russell, Paul Barberin, Willie Santiago, Alnorma Twai on trumpet... She used Paul. She used me.

ctx.x: Can you tell us something about your training and taking lessons and so on?

Well, I started taking lessons around 9 years of age with my uncle, Wooden Joe Nicholas. He was my big influence on this jazz scene. And later on, I went to Papa Teo and took lessons with him for about a couple of years. Then Lorenzo Teo, his son. And finished up with him until around 1915. Then I started to go pro. My first gigs around New Orleans was with the Maple Leaf Band. Then Buddy Petite's Band. When Jimmy Noon left to go to Chicago, I played with Buddy Petite and several other bands around New Orleans.…

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: And just Louie, Pop, and Paul Barberin, and Pop Foster, and Lee Blair, stayed on the stand.

ctx.x: Well, what about Johnny? How did he get interested in music? Do you know? Was he interested? Who? Johnny Dodge. Did you know him when he got interested?

No, when I met Johnny, he was playing. He was playing his head off around 1912. At Betsy Cole. No, Ms. Cole's Lauren. I don't know. We used to say Ms. Cole's Lauren. It used to be penny parties on Sundays, you know, for the youngsters, you know. I was a kid, twelve years old, and I used to go up there. And I was learning time and time, and he was respiring quite a bit. And Johnny was up. And then, of course, I met him to the years. She called. I took his place. And King Howard was playing in 24. When they left…
Mm-hmm. Did the... When you first joined Oliver, who was the trombone player? George Fields. George Fields. George Fields.
